skills.name: Capital letters and sentence endings
skills.rule: Start each sentence with a capital letter and end it with the right mark: full stop, question mark or exclamation mark.

skills.name: Commas in lists
skills.rule: Use commas to separate items in a list. In standard KS2 examples, the final comma before and is usually not needed.
skills.workedBad: We packed torches maps and water.
skills.workedGood: We packed torches, maps and water.
skills.contrastBad: We packed, torches maps, and water.
skills.contrastGood: We packed torches, maps and water.

skills.name: Apostrophes for contraction
skills.rule: Use an apostrophe to show missing letters in contractions, such as can't, didn't and we're.
skills.workedBad: We cant go because were late.
skills.workedGood: We can't go because we're late.
skills.contrastBad: We cant go because we're late.
skills.contrastGood: We can't go because we're late.

skills.name: Apostrophes for possession
skills.rule: Use apostrophes to show belonging: the girl's coat, the girls' coats, the children's books.
skills.workedBad: The girls coat was on the bench.
skills.workedGood: The girl's coat was on the bench.
skills.contrastBad: The girls coat was on the bench.
skills.contrastGood: The girls' coats were on the bench.

skills.name: Inverted commas and speech punctuation
skills.rule: Put spoken words inside inverted commas. Use the correct punctuation inside the closing inverted comma when the punctuation belongs to the spoken words.

skills.name: Commas after fronted adverbials
skills.rule: Put a comma after a starter phrase, such as At last, Before lunch, or Without warning.
skills.workedBad: Before lunch we finished the poster.
skills.workedGood: Before lunch, we finished the poster.
skills.contrastBad: Before lunch we, finished the poster.
skills.contrastGood: Before lunch, we finished the poster.

skills.name: Parenthesis with commas, brackets or dashes
skills.rule: Parenthesis adds extra information. It can be marked with commas, brackets or dashes.
skills.workedBad: Mr Patel our coach arrived early.
skills.workedGood: Mr Patel, our coach, arrived early.
skills.contrastBad: Mr Patel our coach, arrived early.

skills.name: Commas for clarity
skills.rule: A comma can make meaning clearer and avoid ambiguity.
skills.contrastBad: Most of the time travellers worry about delays.
skills.contrastGood: Most of the time, travellers worry about delays.

skills.name: Colon before a list
skills.rule: A colon can introduce a list after a complete opening idea.
skills.workedBad: We needed three things, a torch, a map and a whistle.
skills.workedGood: We needed three things: a torch, a map and a whistle.
skills.contrastBad: We needed: three things a torch, a map and a whistle.
skills.contrastGood: We needed three things: a torch, a map and a whistle.

skills.name: Semi-colons between related clauses
skills.rule: A semi-colon can join two closely related ideas.
skills.workedBad: The rain had stopped, the pitch was still slippery.
skills.workedGood: The rain had stopped; the pitch was still slippery.
skills.contrastBad: The rain had stopped; and the pitch was still slippery.
skills.contrastGood: The rain had stopped; the pitch was still slippery.

skills.name: Dashes between related clauses
skills.rule: A dash can mark a sharp boundary between two closely related ideas.
skills.workedBad: The path was flooded, we took the longer route.
skills.workedGood: The path was flooded – we took the longer route.
skills.contrastBad: The path was flooded –and we took the longer route.
skills.contrastGood: The path was flooded – we took the longer route.

skills.name: Semi-colons within lists
skills.rule: Use semi-colons to separate list items when each item already contains commas.
skills.workedBad: We visited York, England, Cardiff, Wales, and Belfast, Northern Ireland.
skills.workedGood: We visited York, England; Cardiff, Wales; and Belfast, Northern Ireland.
skills.contrastBad: We visited York, England, Cardiff, Wales; and Belfast, Northern Ireland.
skills.contrastGood: We visited York, England; Cardiff, Wales; and Belfast, Northern Ireland.
